seoTitle: Network Connection Info: Online, Speed Class, Data Saver
metaDescription: See what your browser reports about your connection: online status, effective type, estimated downlink and round trip, data saver and live changes.
intro: Read the connection details your browser exposes to web pages and watch them change live.
why:
The Network Information API lets pages adapt to slow or metered connections. This viewer shows what it reports: effective connection type (4g, 3g...), the browser's estimate of downlink and round-trip time, whether data saver is on, and online/offline events, together with logical CPU cores, device memory and languages.

Values are coarse by design (rounded and capped for privacy) and the API exists only in Chromium browsers; Firefox and Safari show a notice. It is not a speed test and cannot reveal your public IP, because that would need a request to a server. Nothing is sent anywhere.
howTo: Open the page; values load immediately.
Switch networks or toggle airplane mode to see the change log update.
Press Refresh to re-read the values.

faq.q: Why are there no values in my browser?
faq.a: Firefox and Safari do not implement the Network Information API.

faq.q: Is the downlink a speed test?
faq.a: No. It is a rounded estimate from recent browser traffic.
No. Looking up a public IP needs a server request, which this tool never makes.
